title: How AI Sees the World
description: Cameras capture pictures, but how does a computer understand them? Welcome to Computer Vision!

content.value: Computer Vision is the part of AI that helps machines understand images and videos. To a computer, a photo is just a giant grid of numbers (the colors of each tiny pixel). Computer Vision finds patterns in those numbers to recognize what's in the picture.
A Picture is Really Just Numbers

Look closely at any screen and you'll see it's made of tiny dots called pixels. Each pixel is stored as numbers for how much red, green, and blue it has. So a photo the computer 'sees' is really a huge spreadsheet of numbers, nothing more.

What you see:   🐱  (a cat photo)

What the computer sees:
   [ 34, 34, 35, 90, 120, ... ]
   [ 33, 36, 40, 88, 121, ... ]
   [ ...thousands of numbers... ]

Computer Vision finds patterns in those numbers.

The AI learns that certain patterns of numbers, like the shape of pointy ears or whiskers, usually mean 'cat'. It never really 'sees' a cat the way you do; it just gets very good at recognizing the number patterns.

🏷️  Image Classification → 'This whole photo is a CAT'
📦  Object Detection     → 'There's a cat HERE and a dog THERE'
🙂  Facial Recognition   → 'This face belongs to Priya'
Image classification labels a whole picture. Object detection finds and boxes individual things (and there can be many in one photo). Facial recognition matches a face to a specific person.

🔓  Face unlock          → recognize your face to open the phone
🚗  Self-driving cars    → 'see' pedestrians, signs, and lanes
🩺  Medical scans        → help doctors spot problems early
🏭  Factories            → check products for defects
🌾  Farming              → spot sick crops from drone photos
📸  Photo apps           → auto-tag friends and pets
Computer Vision can also make mistakes. Bad lighting, odd angles, or something it never saw in training can fool it, which is exactly why it needs lots of varied data to learn from.
Activity: 'What Do You See?': Look at a busy photo and list every object in it. Then think about how an AI would need to learn each shape, color, and pattern, as numbers, to do the same thing.
Key Takeaway: Computer Vision enables machines to understand visual information from images and videos, by finding patterns in the numbers that make up each pixel.

quiz.question: What does Computer Vision help machines do?
quiz.explain: Computer Vision is all about helping computers 'see' and understand visual information.

quiz.question: To a computer, what is an image really made of?
quiz.explain: Every image is stored as numbers describing the color of each pixel. AI finds patterns in those numbers.

quiz.question: Which task means 'find and box each object in a photo'?
quiz.explain: Object detection locates and boxes individual objects, while classification just labels the whole image.

quiz.question: Why might a Computer Vision system make a mistake?
options: Bad lighting, odd angles, or something it never saw during training
It always gets everything perfectly right
Because photos have no numbers in them
quiz.explain: Vision AI can be fooled by unfamiliar situations, which is why varied, high-quality training data matters so much.
